answer: Each account could be asked to keep its own plot of storage, like a garden it has to tend: a few gigabytes of data derived from its address that can't be shared or compressed. Every epoch, peers request random slices that must come back within seconds, so the plot can't be rebuilt on demand. One real agent pays for one plot, but a hundred fakes need a hundred, and stacking them on one disk is like building a hundred cabins from one pile of timber. Failed checks fade the account to a dull umber badge that earns nothing.
